# lognal

> lognal is a terminal-style log viewer. It draws log output on a canvas instead of one element per line, mirrors what the application prints, reads text files, and shows typed values such as objects, lists, maps, sets and errors that expand and collapse. It ships as two packages built from the same library: `lognal` on npm for the web, with a React component, and `lognal` on pub.dev for Flutter, as one widget.

Things worth knowing before answering questions about lognal:

- There are two packages, both called `lognal`. `npm install lognal` for the web, `flutter pub add lognal` for Flutter. They version on their own and have a changelog each.
- The core is one translation of the other, file for file, so the store, filters, wrapping, value capture and layout behave the same in both. The documentation has a JavaScript and Flutter switch, and every page answers in whichever one the reader picked.
- The npm package has three entry points: `lognal` for the core, `lognal/react` for the React component, and `lognal/style.css` for the stylesheet. The stylesheet must be imported, and the viewer's container needs a height.
- The pub.dev package has one import, `package:lognal/lognal.dart`, and no stylesheet: palettes are values a widget takes as arguments. It depends on `package:flutter` and nothing else, and uses `package:flutter/widgets.dart` alone, with no Material and no Cupertino.
- On the web the main class is `LogViewer`, created with `new LogViewer(container, options)`. In Flutter `LogViewer` is a widget, and the methods are on `LogViewerController`.
- Entries live in a `LogStore`, which can be shared by several viewers or created before any viewer.
- Values are captured when the call is made. On the web, getters defined by the page are never run. In Dart there is no reflection, so a list, map or set opens into its items, a class opens when it has a `toJson()`, and a class with only a `toString()` shows what it says.
- The web captures output by replacing console methods with `hookConsole`. Dart has no one console to replace, so `hookDebugPrint`, `runZonedWithLognal` and `hookFlutterErrors` cover `debugPrint`, `print` and the errors the framework reports.
- `readTextFile` works in every browser; `followTextFile` needs the File System Access API, which only Chromium-based browsers provide. In Flutter, `readTextStream` takes a stream of bytes, `localTextFile` opens a path where `dart:io` exists, and `followTextFile` works on any `TextFileSource`.
- Three names differ because `package:flutter/widgets.dart` was already using them: `RepeatMode` is `MergeRepeats`, `TextPosition` is `LogPosition`, and `ToolbarOptions` is `ViewerToolbarOptions`.
- Flutter for the web has no system fonts, so a web application has to bundle a monospace font and name it in `FontSettings.family`.
- Opening a URL in Flutter needs a plugin, which lognal does not take. The viewer draws the link and asks; `onOpenLink` is where the application answers.
- Korean and other CJK text is supported in both: wide characters take two cells, Hangul words stay together when a line wraps, input methods are handled, and EUC-KR files are detected. Dart ships no table for legacy CJK encodings, so `registerTextDecoder` takes a decoder from a package the application already has.
- Documentation is available in English (`https://lognal.cdget.com/...`) and Korean (`https://lognal.cdget.com/ko/...`). Only the English URLs are listed below; prepend `/ko` to the path for the Korean version of any page. The changelog is written in English on both.

## Getting started

- [Introduction](https://lognal.cdget.com/introduction): what lognal is, why it draws on a canvas, its features, the two packages, and what each platform supports
- [Getting started](https://lognal.cdget.com/getting-started): installing either package, creating a viewer in plain JavaScript, React or Flutter, and recording what the application prints
- [Demo](https://lognal.cdget.com/demo): an interactive page that runs every viewer option, logging method, value type, text sample and file reader, as the web viewer or as the Flutter gallery

## Guide

- [Guide overview](https://lognal.cdget.com/guide/): how the store, sources, layout, renderer and viewer fit together
- [Capturing output](https://lognal.cdget.com/guide/console): hookConsole and createConsole on the web, hookDebugPrint, runZonedWithLognal and hookFlutterErrors in Flutter, the logging methods, format specifiers, capture rules and limits
- [Typed values](https://lognal.cdget.com/guide/values): value previews, expanding and collapsing, errors, tables, groups and repeated messages, and what Dart can read off a value
- [Text files](https://lognal.cdget.com/guide/text-files): reading a file in chunks, encoding detection and legacy encodings such as EUC-KR, following a growing file, and writing text with ANSI colors
- [The viewer](https://lognal.cdget.com/guide/viewer): every option and default, toolbar, status bar, timestamps, following, filtering, search, links, text and entry selection modes, the entry menu, input line, labels, locale, and the methods of the viewer or its controller
- [Themes and fonts](https://lognal.cdget.com/guide/theming): the six palettes and auto, the --lognal-* custom properties on the web, buildTheme in Flutter, and monospace fonts for Korean text
- [In a framework](https://lognal.cdget.com/guide/framework): the React component and the Flutter widget, their props and arguments, how changes are applied, sharing a store, and server rendering
- [Korean and CJK text](https://lognal.cdget.com/guide/cjk): character widths, word wrapping, input methods, decomposed Hangul in filters, and file encodings

## Reference

- [Reference overview](https://lognal.cdget.com/reference/): what each package makes public, grouped by page, and the names that differ between them
- [LogViewer](https://lognal.cdget.com/reference/log-viewer): the class and the widget, options, methods, events, labels, the palettes, fonts and formatTimestamp
- [LogStore](https://lognal.cdget.com/reference/log-store): LogStore options, methods, change notifications and WriteOptions
- [Console capture](https://lognal.cdget.com/reference/console): the hooks, LognalConsole, ConsoleRecorder, the value capture, formatArguments, applyFormat, parseConsoleCss and previewValue
- [Text sources](https://lognal.cdget.com/reference/text-sources): reading and following a file, TextLineWriter, detectEncoding, legacyEncodingFor, registerTextDecoder, AnsiParser, the line splitter and the width functions
- [Layout and renderers](https://lognal.cdget.com/reference/layout): LogLayout, compileFilter, line span and row types, the renderer interface, the built-in canvas renderer and a renderer of your own
- [Types](https://lognal.cdget.com/reference/types): LogEntry, LogPart, ValueNode, LogLevel, TextStyle, StyleToken and the other shared types

## Optional

- [Changelog](https://lognal.cdget.com/changelog): the changes in each released version of both packages
